newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London-based Arab newspapers - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London-based Arab newspapers - Sept 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in two London-based Arabic-language newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwaiti foreign minister Sheikh Sabah says ousting Iraqi President Saddam from power is not a Kuwaiti duty.
- Arab Investment Company discusses Algeria's membership, decides to invest in privatised Egyptian projects.
- Gulf Arab states await investors' bids to finance a proposed project to link their power grid.
- Thousands of tourists cancel bookings to Jordan because of the situation in the West Bank and Gaza. At least 69 people were killed in clashes between Israel and Palestinians.
- Qatar welcomes Bahrain's decision to send a memorandum to the International Court of Justice in the Hague. Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a territorial dispute.
- Three Saudi cement companies settle disputes with a German contracting company over contracts worth three billion riyals to build new cement plants.
- Steps to link bourses of Kuwait, Egypt and Lebanon are expected to be completed before the end of the year.
